title: KP14 with a priced OU volatility factor and three firm types with exponential exposure
question: Does premium-side extremity in the priced-vol channel create both room and capture?
notes: Current runnable spec for the vyx economy. Parameters are unchanged from v1 and still match variants/kp_vy/run_vyx.sh; what changed is the ECONOMY those parameters produce, via the lambda regime-label fix. v1's published figures (room +0.3496, gap_RFF-lin +0.1009, t 21.6, rank 1 of 24) therefore describe a different economy and must NOT be quoted for this one. No figures are published here yet: the first clean run has not been made. Premia approx 4.6/12/22 pct per year under v1's labels; not re-derived under the corrected ones.

changes: kp_regime_labels legacy_swapped -> corrected: mu_H/mu_L are ENTRY rates, so P(high) = mu_H/(mu_H+mu_L) = 0.3191. v1 ran at E[lambda] = 1.7172 instead of the intended 1.0. This is a DIFFERENT ECONOMY, which is why v1 is superseded rather than corrected in place.
kp_cir_quadrature epsrel 1e-10 -> 1e-6: 1e-10 was unattainable for QUADPACK, which subdivided to the limit and warned; tables move ~4e-7.
G stage now a direct sparse solve instead of a 1e6-iteration implicit Euler (0.10 s/type vs ~2 h, relative residual ~8e-13).
records expected_solves, so a run can verify by content that it built the economy this spec describes.

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the pre-2026-09-07 single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the old fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
